title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §2.6 of the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. For an abelian scheme f: A → S, the previous page introduced Serre's universal vector extension G(A) = E(A), the extension 0 → V(t_{A'}) → G(A) → A → 0. Its Lie algebra is the extension 0 → t^∨_{A*} → g(A) → t_A → 0, which is the dual of the Hodge filtration on H^1_DR(A/S). This page states the conjectured refinements of assertions 1° and 3° of 2.4–2.5.

(1° refined) There should be a crystal in smooth group schemes G(A/S) on S. For every infinitesimal lifting B of A over a thickening T of S it should come with a canonical isomorphism G(A/S)(T) ≅ G(B/T). This should be functorial in A and compatible with base change. In modern terms, the universal vector extension is a crystal in groups and depends only on A, not on the chosen lift. This is the content of Mazur–Messing (1974), on PD-thickenings with nilpotent divided powers.

(3° refined) The quasi-inverse of the functor 'lifts of A ↦ lifts of the Hodge filtration' is described explicitly. Extending the filtration of DR^1(A/S)(S) to a filtration of the Lie algebra DR^1(A/S)(T)^∨ of G(A/S)(T) is the same as extending the canonical vector subgroup V(t_{A'}) ⊂ G(A/S)(S) to a vector subgroup of G(A/S)(T). The lift B is then recovered as the quotient G(A/S)(T)/(extended vector subgroup). This is exactly the Grothendieck–Messing form of deformation theory: lifts correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration in the crystal, with the abelian scheme recovered as a quotient of the universal extension.

NB (origin of the idea). Grothendieck says he found the canonical connection on G(A/S) while trying to simplify Manin's construction (1963, Mordell over function fields; 'theorem of the kernel') of the map A(S) → Γ(S, O_S) attached to a Picard–Fuchs equation. The construction runs as follows:
- Locally on S, a section P of A lifts to a section P~ of G, since the obstruction lies in H^1(S, vector bundle), which vanishes on affines.
- The connection on G gives a logarithmic derivative ∇P~ ∈ Γ(S, t_G ⊗ Ω^1_S). This is well defined up to the derivatives of sections of the vector part t^∨_{A*}, reflecting the choice of lift.
- This 1-form is closed (horizontal) for the Gauss–Manin connection on t_G = H^1_DR^∨.
- Applying the Picard–Fuchs operator, which kills exactly that indeterminacy, yields a function in O_S.

This is the modern 'Manin map via the universal vector extension and its logarithmic derivative', as in Coleman 1990, Chai 1991, Buium and Bertrand. He restricts to characteristic 0, as Manin does. The next page then records which cases he has verified (char 0, first-order thickenings, rigidity of G(A)). It also shows that the naive version (absolute stratification, without divided powers) is false in characteristic p, because of supersingular (Hasse-invariant-zero) curves.
errors: As stated for arbitrary infinitesimal prolongations (no divided-power structure), assertion 1° cannot hold in characteristic p. The next page (2.7) itself shows that a functorial stratification on H^1_DR fails, and margin notes mark b) as 'faux'. The correct statement needs PD-thickenings, as in Mazur–Messing and Grothendieck–Messing.

Minor imprecision: the indeterminacy of ∇P~ is not 'a section of the image of t^∨_{A*}' as such. It is the image under d/∇ of sections of the vector part, i.e. the log-derivatives of sections of V(t_{A'}). The Picard–Fuchs operator is what kills these.
'Picart-Fuchs' is a misspelling of Picard–Fuchs (corrected once by hand in the typescript).

ideas.what: Universal vector extension E(A) of an abelian scheme forms a crystal in groups; its value on a thickening T is E(B) for any lift B
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline nature of the universal vector extension (Dieudonné crystal of A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, 1966 letter to Tate / 1970 ICM); proved by Mazur–Messing 1974
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, ICM Nice 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés); Montréal 1970 lectures

ideas.what: Lifts of A to T correspond to extending the vector subgroup of E(A)(T); B is recovered as the quotient
ideas.where_published: ICM 1970 report; Montréal lecture notes 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

ideas.what: Manin's map A(S) → O_S constructed by lifting sections to the universal vector extension and taking the logarithmic derivative via its canonical connection, then applying Picard–Fuchs
ideas.modern_name: Manin map / Manin homomorphism via universal vector extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin 1963; reformulation via universal vector extension by Coleman (1990), Chai (1991), Buium, Bertrand
ideas.where_published: Possibly only in this letter to Tate (circulated); not in EGA/SGA as far as I know

missed.claim: Already in 1966 Grothendieck sketched the reinterpretation of Manin's 'theorem of the kernel' map as the logarithmic derivative of a lift to the universal vector extension, using its Gauss–Manin connection, followed by a Picard–Fuchs operator. This is the formulation later popularized by Coleman (1990) and Chai (1991). He also says this is how he discovered the canonical connection on G(A), i.e. the crystal structure.
missed.quote: Je suis tombé sur la connexion canonique de G(A/S) en essayant de simplifier la construction de Manin de l'application A(S) → Γ(S,O_S) associée à une équation de Picart-Fuchs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: the Manin-map literature (Coleman, Chai, Bertrand, Buium, Bertrand–Pillay) does not generally credit Grothendieck's 1966 letter. It also documents that crystalline Dieudonné theory originated from a diophantine motivation.

deep.surprise_reason: The crystal and deformation statements are Grothendieck's well-known 1966–70 program, proved by Messing and Mazur–Messing. The NB is a modest but genuine historical detail: an early, apparently uncredited universal-vector-extension version of the Manin map, presented as the origin of the canonical connection.

'sur S?' — the typed character after S looks like an overstruck '.'/'?'; read 'sur S.'
The struck-through word before t_G ⊗ Ω^1_S is illegible ('xxx'); 'un [c]cycle' has a handwritten 'cycle' underlined.
'DR^1(A/S)(S)': the typed 'S' is overstruck on another letter in the original.
